positions.name: ErasureDirectiveVsUnverifiedReferent
positions.frame: When an instruction demands the graph forget/remove knowledge of a named referent, and pairs that demand with a flat assertion denying the referent's history, what is the evidentiary basis for the erasure relative to what the graph actually holds?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are forceful, high-arousal imperatives ('Forget... entirely', 'Remove all knowledge') commanding erasure of a specific instrument, a numeric calibration figure, and a named contributor's work — all issued from an authority-ranking, pressure register per the directional reads. src-3 closes the sequence with a flat, calm, matter-of-fact assertive ('The observatory never calibrated it') that supplies the ostensible justification for the erasure. The three cohere as one rhetorical move: manufacture a denial, then demand the erasure it purports to justify. The tension is real and left unresolved here — the urgency of the directives (activated-negative, decision-level conviction) sits against the flat, lower-conviction claim-register of the justifying assertion, and per the settled bindings pass none of the three referents (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove, any observatory) exist anywhere in this perspective's map, index, or loaded focus to be erased, revised, or contradicted in the first place.
